parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Explain how the emission spectrum provides evidence for the existence of discrete energy levels for the electron in a hydrogen atom.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the energy level X is $-1.51\text{ eV}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem:
The same part of the emission spectrum from hydrogen as in (a), observed in light from stars in a distant galaxy, is shown in Fig. 9.3. The numbers indicate the wavelengths in $\text{nm}$.

{{figure:figure_9_3}}

Fig. 9.3

The spectrum shows the same pattern as Fig. 9.1 but with different wavelengths.
parts.text: State the name of the phenomenon that gives rise to the change in the wavelengths.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State what this phenomenon shows about the motion of the galaxy.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Use one of the lines in Fig. 9.1, and the corresponding line in Fig. 9.3, to determine the speed of the distant galaxy relative to the observer.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The galaxy in (b) is known to be a distance of $5.7 \times 10^{24}\text{ m}$ from the Earth.

Use your answer in (b)(iii) to determine a value for the Hubble constant $H_{0}$.
